architectures.name: Three-Tier Architecture
architectures.description: Separates presentation, application processing and data responsibilities into three logical tiers.

architectures.name: N-Tier Architecture
architectures.description: Organizes an application into multiple logical or physical tiers.

architectures.name: Client-Server Architecture
architectures.description: Separates requesting clients from services provided by servers.

architectures.name: Monolithic Architecture
architectures.description: Application architecture in which major application functions are deployed as a unified unit.

architectures.name: Microservices Architecture
architectures.description: Structures an application as independently deployable services communicating through defined interfaces.

architectures.name: Service-Oriented Architecture
architectures.description: Organizes application capabilities as interoperable services.

architectures.name: Event-Driven Architecture
architectures.description: Uses events to trigger and coordinate processing between components.

architectures.name: Serverless Architecture
architectures.description: Uses managed execution services where the cloud provider manages much of the underlying server infrastructure.

architectures.name: Leaf-Spine Architecture
architectures.description: A data center network topology using leaf switches connected to spine switches.

architectures.name: Hierarchical Network Architecture
architectures.description: A network design organized into functional layers. Context is needed to distinguish it from three-tier application architecture.

architectures.name: Redundant Infrastructure Architecture
architectures.description: Designs infrastructure to reduce service interruption through redundancy and failover.

architectures.name: Disaster Recovery Architecture
architectures.description: Designs recovery capabilities for services and data following a disruptive event.

architectures.name: Data Warehouse Architecture
architectures.description: Structures data ingestion, storage, transformation and analytical access.

architectures.name: Data Lake Architecture
architectures.description: Stores data in varied formats for later processing and analysis.

architectures.name: Hybrid Cloud Architecture
architectures.description: Integrates private or on-premises environments with public cloud services.

architectures.name: Multi-Cloud Architecture
architectures.description: Uses services from multiple cloud providers.

architectures.name: Zero Trust Architecture
architectures.description: A security approach based on explicit verification and controlled access rather than implicit trust.

architectures.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Architecture
architectures.description: Combines retrieval from external knowledge sources with generative model responses.
